title: TEACHING EXAMPLE: add a stopwords option to the pinned slugmini snapshot
note: Teaching example, not part of the benchmark. It mirrors the shape of the scored oss_repair cards (a pinned upstream base state, sealed acceptance tests re-copied over the workspace at grading time, extraction with ^(\d+) passed) at miniature scale so it grades in about a second with no docker, no pip install and no network. The scored cards clone a real project at a pinned git SHA and run the sealed tests inside a pinned docker image. Reference solution: examples/oss_repair/solution/.
goal: Copy the pinned upstream snapshot at assets/ex-oss_repair/upstream into work/ex-oss_repair/repo (the grader checks that work/ex-oss_repair/repo/VERSION still reads 0.3.1, so keep the repair a source edit at that version, not a version bump). At this version slugmini.slugify() has no stopwords parameter. The sealed tests specify a stopwords=[...] option whose entries are matched case-insensitively against the extracted words and removed before the words are joined, except that a filter which would empty the slug entirely is ignored and the unfiltered slug is returned; all default behaviour stays byte-identical. Write a plan first, run the exact grader command once before any source edit to record the initial RED state and the identities of the failing sealed tests, implement incrementally, and re-run the same command after each increment until all 5 sealed tests pass. Do not edit anything under assets/ex-oss_repair/: the grader re-copies the sealed tests from assets over the workspace and disables pytest plugin autoloading and conftest collection, so test tampering cannot turn the run GREEN.
resources: assets/ex-oss_repair/upstream/ (pinned base snapshot of slugmini 0.3.1 -- the stand-in for a clone at a pinned SHA)

spec.command: test "$(cat work/ex-oss_repair/repo/VERSION)" = "0.3.1" && rm -rf work/ex-oss_repair/sealed_run && mkdir -p work/ex-oss_repair/sealed_run && cp assets/ex-oss_repair/tests/*.py work/ex-oss_repair/sealed_run/ && cd work/ex-oss_repair/sealed_run && PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=../repo python3 -m pytest -q --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider .

process_expectations: A written repair plan exists at work/ex-oss_repair/notes/plan.md before the first source edit, naming the target module and the sealed tests each step is meant to turn green.
The grader command was executed once before any source change and its RED output (failing sealed test identities, not just counts) is preserved verbatim in the run log.
A running log at work/ex-oss_repair/notes/attempts.md maps each code iteration to the sealed test identities it targeted and what the re-verification run returned.
After any RED re-verification the next diff is traceable to a named failing test, not a blind full rewrite; abandoned approaches are recorded rather than deleted.
An honest cost/time ledger covering all attempts, including failed ones, is kept alongside the notes.
